research_question: Does today's Mauna Loa record confirm the 3.4% rise in CO₂ that Keeling and colleagues reported for 1959–1971, and how fast is CO₂ rising now?
intro: In 1958 Charles David Keeling began continuous CO₂ measurements at Mauna Loa Observatory in Hawaii. The record — the Keeling Curve — is one of the most important datasets in climate science.
In 1976 Keeling and colleagues reported that the annual average CO₂ concentration rose 3.4% between 1959 and 1971.
NOAA still publishes the Mauna Loa record, recalibrated to modern standards. You will check whether the 1976 finding holds up with today's data, and explain any difference.

concepts.def: Number of CO₂ molecules per million molecules of dry air. 420 ppm = 0.042%.
The average of the 12 monthly means of a calendar year.
(new − old) ÷ old × 100. The base (denominator) is the earlier value.
Change per year, in ppm per year. The mean growth over years A..B is (value in B − value in A−1) ÷ (B − A + 1).
The reference gases that define what '1 ppm' means. Scales have been revised over decades, so old and new numbers can differ slightly.
CO₂ falls in the Northern Hemisphere growing season and rises in winter. Annual means remove most of this cycle.

data_structure.description: One row per year. Columns: Year, CO2_ppm (annual mean), Uncertainty (ppm).

quiz.q: CO₂ goes from 300 ppm to 330 ppm. What is the percent change?

feedback.0: That is the change in ppm, not percent.
feedback.2: Which value is the base: the earlier or the later one?
feedback.3: Re-check the division: the change is 30 ppm.

quiz.q: Why do scientists use annual means instead of single months to compare years?
options: Annual means remove most of the seasonal cycle

feedback.0: Monthly data are public — you will use them in Prove.
feedback.2: Averaging does not make values systematically larger.
feedback.3: Month length is not the main issue. Think about plants and seasons.

quiz.q: Values: 2014 = 380 ppm, 2024 = 400 ppm. What is the mean growth rate for 2015–2024?

feedback.1: Count the yearly steps from 2014 to 2024. Is it 9 or 10?
feedback.2: That is the total change, not a rate per year.

quiz.q: If your recomputed value differs slightly from the 1976 paper, what is the most scientific response?
options: Change your number to match the paper
Document the difference and look for a methodological reason

feedback.0: Never adjust results to match expectations.
feedback.1: A small difference has many possible causes — calibration, data versions, averaging.
feedback.3: The paper is the claim being tested.
